---
title: "00 — Run the complete future-year study"
output: html_notebook
---

Each time this master notebook is run, it allocates the next persistent run number and executes the numbered stage notebooks in order. The stages all share the same increment.

The study first audits the BRFSS inputs, then prepares time-ordered data,
validates candidate models on earlier survey years, selects a national model
with 2023 data, calibrates probabilities with 2024 data, and evaluates the
frozen workflow on 2025 data. The final stages summarize subgroup performance
and prespecified descriptive or sensitivity analyses without changing the
selected model.

## Initialize project and increment

Reads shared settings, allocates a unique run number, and creates empty output directories. Models from prior runs are never reused.

```{r initialize-project-and-increment}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Project-root discovery
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Searches upward from the current working directory for the project file.
# Allows the notebook to locate the project when started from a subfolder.
find_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
    current <- normalizePath(start, mustWork = TRUE)

    repeat {
        # Directory containing this file is the project root if it has the RStudio
        # project file.
        if (file.exists(file.path(current, "FMD_Project.Rproj"))) {
            return(current)
        }

        parent <- dirname(current)

        if (identical(parent, current)) {
            stop("Open FMD_Project.Rproj in RStudio first")
        }

        current <- parent
    }
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Notebook working-directory configuration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Resolves project location before constructing any module or output paths.
project_root <- find_project_root()

# Uses the project root as the working directory for subsequent chunks
# evaluated by knitr.
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = project_root)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared-module loader
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Extract and execute R code chunks from a shared R Markdown module.
# Evaluate the code in each notebooks environment so functions and
# configuration variables are available to the calling notebook.
load_module <- function(name) {
    path <- file.path(
        project_root,
        "R",
        paste0(name, ".Rmd")
    )

    text <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)

    # Identify opening R chunk fences and standalone closing fences.
    # Assumes the shared modules use this format.
    starts <- which(startsWith(text, "```{r"))
    ends <- which(trimws(text) == "```")

    # Collect the code between each R opening fence and the next closing fence.
    blocks <- lapply(starts, function(start) {
        finish <- ends[ends > start][1]

        # Require a closing fence and at least one intervening line.
        if (is.na(finish) || finish <= start + 1L) {
            stop("Missing code or closing fence in ", path)
        }

        paste(
            text[(start + 1L):(finish - 1L)],
            collapse = "\n"
        )
    })

    # Combine the extracted chunks in their original order, parse the R code,
    # and execute it in the environment that called load_module().
    eval(
        parse(text = paste(blocks, collapse = "\n\n")),
        envir = parent.frame()
    )

    invisible(TRUE)
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared configuration and utilities
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Load configuration first so the remaining modules can use shared settings.
# The run manager defines run-allocation and artifact-management functions.
# The helpers module defines validation, modeling, and metric utilities.
load_module("config")
load_module("run_manager")
load_module("helpers")


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Analysis dependency check
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Verify the packages required by this workflow before allocating a new run.
# check_packages() stops with instructions if a dependency is unavailable;
# it does not install packages.
check_packages(c(
    "data.table",
    "ggplot2",
    "glmnet",
    "ranger",
    "Matrix",
    "survey",
    "rmarkdown",
    "scales"
))


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fresh run allocation
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Discard an inherited or leftover run ID before starting a complete execution.
# This prevents the master notebook from reusing that ID.
if (nzchar(Sys.getenv("ATG_RUN_ID", unset = ""))) {
    Sys.unsetenv("ATG_RUN_ID")
}

# Allocates one new persistent increment and publishes its environment variable.
# Stage notebooks attach to the run.
run_id <- start_new_run()

# Resolve the new run's directories for the artifact-saving helpers.
run_context <- attach_run()


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Run confirmation
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Display the allocated increment in the notebook output for traceability.
cat("[NEW STUDY RUN] Increment", run_id, "\n")
```


## Render the notebook stages

Executes preprocessing, optional PCA, temporal model development, 2023 selection, 2024 calibration, 2025 evaluation, AI/AN auditing, sensitivity checks, and the research summary. Every created graph prints in its notebook.

```{r render-the-notebook-stages}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Core notebook sequence
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Defines stages in execution order.
# Earlier stages prepare the data and modeling artifacts used by later stages.
stage_names <- c(
    "01_Audit_Data.Rmd",
    "02_Prepare_Annual_Sets.Rmd",
    "03_Class_PCA_Optional.Rmd",
    "04_Forward_Year_Validation.Rmd",
    "05_Select_Model_2023.Rmd",
    "05b_Feature_Group_Analysis.Rmd",
    "06_Calibrate_2024.Rmd",
    "07_Evaluate_2025.Rmd",
    "08_AI_AN_Equity_Evaluation.Rmd",
    "09_Sensitivity_Analysis.Rmd",
    "11_Annual_Shifts.Rmd"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# For Optional diagnostic stages
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Append the PSU-bootstrap analysis only when enabled in the configuration.
if (run_psu_bootstrap) {
    stage_names <- c(
        stage_names,
        "12_PSU_Bootstrap_AUROC.Rmd"
    )
}

# Append the 2023 predictor-permutation analysis only when enabled.
if (run_predictor_permutation) {
    stage_names <- c(
        stage_names,
        "13_2023_Permutation_Importance.Rmd"
    )
}

# Run the additional insight notebooks in the same numbered execution. Notebook 14
# links these stages to the current run.
stage_names <- c(
    stage_names,
    "14_Run_Additional_Insights.Rmd"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Final synthesis stage
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Runs the findings summary last so it can use outputs from all preceding
# stages, includes whichever optional diagnostics were enabled.
stage_names <- c(
    stage_names,
    "10_Summarize_Findings.Rmd"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sequential notebook rendering
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Render one stage at a time so upstream outputs are available before
# downstream notebooks begin. Every rendered HTML file is written to the
# active run's notebooks directory.
for (stage_name in stage_names) {
    # Locate the source notebook within the project.
    input_file <- file.path(
        project_root,
        "notebooks",
        stage_name
    )

    # Give the rendered notebook the same run suffix as the other artifacts.
    output_file <- sprintf(
        "%s_run_%s.nb.html",
        tools::file_path_sans_ext(stage_name),
        run_context$id
    )

    target <- file.path(run_context$notebooks, output_file)

    # Pre-render existence check.
    # Stops to not replace notebook run output.
    if (file.exists(target)) {
        stop("Stage output already exists: ", target)
    }

    # Identifies the stage and run in the master notebook's progress output.
    cat(
        "\n[NOTEBOOK] ",
        stage_name,
        " | run ",
        run_context$id,
        "\n",
        sep = ""
    )

    # Render into the current run's notebook directory; no stage HTML is
    # written beside the source Rmd file.
    #
    # Use the project root for chunk execution so relative project paths
    # resolve consistently across stages.
    #
    # Provides each stage a fresh evaluation environment. Parent is the
    # global environment, so global objects remain accessible.
    #
    # Keep rendering messages visible to support progress checks and debugging.
    rmarkdown::render(
        input = input_file,
        output_file = output_file,
        output_dir = run_context$notebooks,
        knit_root_dir = project_root,
        envir = new.env(parent = globalenv()),
        quiet = FALSE
    )

    # Garbage collection after each successfully rendered stage.
    # Objects that remain referenced are not removed.
    gc(verbose = FALSE)
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Successful-completion message
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# This point is reached only if every selected render call finishes
# without an unhandled error.
cat(
    "\n[FINISHED] All outputs for increment ",
    run_context$id,
    " saved.\n",
    sep = ""
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Session cleanup
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Clears the environment-based run ID after successful completion.
Sys.unsetenv("ATG_RUN_ID")
```
